summary.headline: BPCL Q2 FY27 standalone PAT rose to INR4,993 crore from a Q1 loss of INR3,962 crore, despite Brent averaging about $116 in September.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone PAT was INR4,993 crore against a Q1 standalone loss of INR3,962 crore, with revenue from operations of about INR1.5 lakh crore. Management attributed the recovery to agile crude sourcing, a Q2 refining GRM of $32.53/bbl (about $14 after SAED), and lower LPG under-recoveries, which fell to about INR290/cylinder from INR507. Standalone gross borrowings fell to INR15,246 crore and the debt-to-equity ratio improved to 0.16. Marketing under-recoveries on petrol and diesel were still a drag, and management said there was no further discussion on marketing margin improvement at this point.

segments.name: Refining
segments.commentary: Throughput 10.4 MMT in Q2 at 117% capacity utilisation; distillate yield 84.38%. Q1 throughput was 10.15 MMT. Management said Q2 GRM fell on higher crude freight and loss of Russian discounts on high-sulphur grades.

segments.name: Marketing
segments.commentary: Domestic sales 13.47 MMT in Q2 vs 13.62 MMT in Q1. Outlets rose to 25,592 from 25,485. Speed 100 at 162 outlets; BeCafe at 234 locations. Marketing under-recoveries were a drag on Q2 earnings.

segments.name: LPG
segments.commentary: Under-recovery per cylinder by month: July INR490, August INR179, September INR199, October expected INR245, November expected INR328. US-origin cargoes were about 48% of Q2 LPG imports; 32 days of inventory held. Government subsidy of about INR632 crore/month for BPCL ended in October 2026.

segments.name: Gas
segments.commentary: Bulk gas record H1 sales of 979 TMT (+53% YoY); CGD sales 177 TMT (+65% YoY). CBG blending 6.5% in H1 vs 3% mandate. LNG long-term contracts under force majeure; spot cargoes sourced from US, Oman and West Africa.

segments.name: Upstream (BPRL)
segments.commentary: Mozambique 47% complete; first gas mid-2028 (June/July). BPCL share of Phase 1 about 1.3 MMT/yr from 13 MMT, with total share of about 4.2-4.5 MMT if all three trains are developed. Brazil BM-SEAL-11 FPSO awarded May 2026; first oil FY31, first gas FY32.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex target of INR25,000 crore retained, with management saying it may rise slightly if project progress is good.
FY28-FY29 capex guided at INR40,000-45,000 crore, excluding the Andhra Pradesh refinery.

Andhra Pradesh 10 MMT refinery with 32-33% petrochemical intensity: board approval for a wholly owned project company with authorised capital up to INR4,900 crore; FID expected in 2-3 weeks subject to CCEA approval, with approvals in 3-4 months.
Planned Mumbai and Bina turnarounds in Q3/Q4 mean throughput will likely not stay at 118% utilisation; Kochi shutdown 30-40 days.
Expects about 6 MMT of product imports from other refineries by end-FY27, with 89.27% MS and 79.34% HSD self-sourced from own refineries.
Crude supply tied up through December 2026; 22 days of crude inventory at 30 Sep 2026.
capex_capacity: Bina Petrochemical and refinery expansion: 40.2% complete, approved cost INR43,367 crore, INR7,566 crore incurred, commissioning mid-FY28, no revision.
Kochi polypropylene: 55.1% complete, approved INR4,850 crore, scheduled completion October 2027 (as stated).
Mumbai PRFCC: INR13,626 crore project, 9.2% complete, INR130 crore spent in Q2; scheduled completion stated as September 2029 in Q1 call.
SAF co-processing at Mumbai: phase 1 kerosene hydrotreater revamp targeted for commissioning January 2027.
Mozambique cumulative spend about $2.8 billion, with $1.8 billion more to come; total investment about $4.5-4.6 billion including exploration. Project finance at 6-8.5%.
demand_pricing: Diesel demand growth expected at 3.5-4% and MS at 5-6% over the medium term, per management outlook.
Russian crude premium narrowed to $1-2/bbl over benchmark for December offers, from $12-13 in October.
Dated Brent around $125-127 in early November vs ICE Brent near $115; most BPCL term contracts priced on dated Brent, so crude cost rises with dated Brent.
ATF: international segment fully passed through; domestic ATF losses not quantified; ATF sales split about 55-60% international.
Retail outlet additions about 1,000/yr; capex of about INR500 crore per 1,000 ROs.

qa_highlights.question: Has the crude sourcing mix changed in October, and how is the mix through December?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East volumes increased, including via Yanbu and ADNOC cargoes; Iraq and Kuwait not yet full. Russian volumes fell in November on freight and premiums, with a few December cargoes possible.

qa_highlights.question: Landed crude cost versus benchmark?
qa_highlights.answer: Benchmark plus $10-12 currently, versus $4-5 pre-war and $13-15 in Q1 2026, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is any change to marketing margins being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: No further discussion on marketing margin improvement; monthly review of under-recoveries; integrated profitability is near normal levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 GRM fall vs Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Crude freight costs rose sharply and Russian discounts disappeared on some high-sulphur cargoes; gasoline and gasoil spreads were broadly flat versus Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR150 crore higher transport cost, INR150 crore higher octroi and taxes, and about INR1,200-1,300 crore MTM losses on hedges of forward spreads.

qa_highlights.question: Does FY28-29 capex include the Andhra Pradesh refinery?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Mozambique and Brazil are included; AP refinery will be added once FID is approved, with capex rework to follow.

risks_watch: Standalone marketing losses persist with petrol and diesel under-recoveries; management said a standard margin is not yet defined and no retail price improvement is under discussion.
LPG compensation support (INR17,334 crore buffer) depends on government budgetary support; timing unclear; the prior subsidy of about INR632 crore/month ended in October 2026.
Dated Brent vs ICE Brent spread and freight/insurance premiums add to crude cost; Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea disruptions remain.
Leverage peak under the AP refinery and FY28-29 capex of INR40,000-45,000 crore; management targets peak standalone debt-to-equity around 1.
Bina expansion progress and cost, with 20-25% of work yet to be awarded as of the earlier Q4 call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and balance sheet but cautious on pricing: management repeatedly said the war is unresolved and it cannot give timelines for LPG support or marketing margin relief. Evasive on Q3-Q4 refining margin and inventory gain/loss questions, saying these are not calculated.
key_quotes: Once this war resolves, crude cannot command at this price because the supplies are there, supplies are there, production is there.
There is no further discussions on any improvement on the marketing margins at this point of time.
We are expecting maybe in next 2-3 weeks we will take it to the board for a final investment decision, subject to financial closure and subject to CCEA approval.
Overall, against our FY26-'27 capex target of INR25,000 crores, we have incurred INR13,749 crores during the first half, including INR9,300 crores in Q2.

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; FY27 capex held at INR25,000 crore and FY28-29 capex guided at INR40,000-45,000 crore, with Bina expansion (commissioning mid-FY28) and Kochi PP (Oct 2027) as the main capacity additions, while Q2 utilisation is 117% and Mumbai/Bina turnarounds are planned for Q3/Q4.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 GRM fell to $32.53/bbl (about $14 after SAED) from $41.41 in Q1, marketing under-recoveries persist, and management said no further discussion on marketing margin improvement; LPG under-recovery still about INR290/cylinder with Nov expected at INR328.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q4 FY28 (Bina); Q4 FY27-Q4 FY28 for Kochi PP
rows.why: Bina petrochemical and refinery expansion (40.2% complete, INR43,367 crore, commissioning mid-FY28) and Kochi PP (55.1% complete, scheduled October 2027) are under construction, but these fall largely outside the 2-4 quarter window and Mumbai PRFCC is only 9.2% complete with Sept 2029 target.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Refining ran at 117% utilisation (10.4 MMT in Q2) but Mumbai and Bina turnarounds in Q3/Q4 and a 30-40 day Kochi shutdown mean throughput will likely not stay at that level; domestic sales slipped to 13.47 MMT from 13.62 MMT.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board approved a wholly owned Andhra Pradesh 10 MMT project company with authorised capital up to INR4,900 crore, FID expected in 2-3 weeks subject to CCEA approval; FY28-29 capex guided at INR40,000-45,000 crore excluding AP, and utilisation at 117% supports further capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management could not give timelines for LPG support or marketing margin relief, the war is unresolved, and dated Brent (~$125-127) is well above ICE Brent (~$115), raising crude cost.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Marketing under-recoveries persist, LPG subsidy of about INR632 crore/month ended in October 2026, and Q3-Q4 turnarounds reduce throughput; FY27 capex may rise 5-10% if progress is good, and peak standalone D/E around 1 is targeted.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: SAF co-processing phase 1 kerosene hydrotreater revamp at Mumbai targeted for commissioning January 2027; no other new product launches discussed.

rows.label: LPG compensation buffer and government support
rows.why: Cumulative LPG compensation buffer of INR17,334 crore at 30 Sep 2026 after INR3,796 crore received in H1, but timing of further support is unclear and the INR632 crore/month subsidy ended in October 2026.

rows.label: Russian crude discount recovery
rows.why: Russian premium narrowed to $1-2/bbl over benchmark for December offers from $12-13 in October, though Russian volumes fell in November and only a few December cargoes are possible.

rows.label: Standalone gross borrowings and D/E
rows.why: Gross borrowings fell to INR15,246 crore from INR17,386 crore and D/E to 0.16 from 0.19, but net borrowings rose to INR7,106 crore from INR4,800 crore and management targets peak D/E near 1 with AP refinery and FY28-29 capex.

tone.note: Management was confident on operations, crude sourcing and the balance sheet, but cautious on pricing, giving no timeline for LPG support or marketing margin relief; it was evasive on Q3-Q4 refining margins and inventory gain/loss, and analysts pressed on marketing losses and the leverage path.
